Subject: Order form redlines — IP & training rights (NovaTek)

Alex / Hannah,

Thanks for the quick sync earlier. Per our conversation I’m attaching our latest redline (Novatek_OrderForm_redline_v3.pdf) that narrows the IP/feedback language and proposes a middle path on model training. High level:

- Output ownership: we’re preserving customer ownership of customer-provided content and outputs generated directly from that content, but asking for a narrow feedback license so we can improve service quality (non-identifying, aggregated).
- Training/data use: customer data used for product improvements must be de-identified and subject to a telemetry tag; opt-out available via order form Exhibit A.
- Feedback license: limited, non-exclusive, revocable for specific datasets; we also offer an audit/evidence pathway for larger accounts.

Could you review the attached and confirm whether procurement needs different redline positions (e.g., explicit assignment requests from legal)? If you think we need to move faster I can escalate to Ben in legal for a proposed compromise language.

Attachments: Novatek_OrderForm_redline_v3.pdf (pdf) — tracked changes; Redline_Summary_notes.docx (docx) — short rationale per clause.

Next steps: if procurement is okay with the compromise points, we’ll produce a clean counterproposal for signature and send SOC2 evidence (SOC2_Type2_stub.pdf) for your security review.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen

Subject: Re: Order form redlines — IP & training rights (NovaTek)

Stephanie, thanks for sending. We reviewed the redline and have two immediate asks before procurement can greenlight:

1) Can you be explicit that the feedback license excludes direct retraining of customer-specific models or customer training datasets unless we sign an additional Data Use Addendum? Procurement wants a clear opt-in for retrain.
2) We need SOC2 evidence and a short description of the telemetry/metadata tags you propose; security wants concrete fields we’ll see in logs (no personal data).

Hannah (our GC) flagged the assignment language — our legal team will likely push for assignment of deliverables created by your models in certain uses. That could block procurement unless we get a clear commercial concession.

Can your team propose precise language that addresses these two asks? If you prefer, we can route a final redline through DocuSign once language is settled.

Cheers,
Alex
Alex Chow
Sr. Procurement Manager, NovaTek
alex.chow@novatek.com

Ben / Karthik — FYI and action request. NovaTek (Alex + Hannah) pushed back on two items: explicit opt-in for retrain and clarity on assignment of deliverables. Procurement wants language that blocks assignment-based claims on outputs without commercial concession.

Summary of asks from Alex:
- Make the feedback license explicit: non-identifiable + excludes retrain unless a signed Data Use Addendum exists.
- Provide a short, security-friendly description of telemetry tags and confirm we will supply SOC2 evidence.
- Consider a commercial concession: holdback on assignment requests or limited-use carveout for productization at a higher tier.

Proposed plan:
1) Legal drafts two short clauses — one for feedback/training carveout (single paragraph) and one for deliverables assignment narrow carveout (single paragraph). Keep it acceptable to sales: avoid full assignment.
2) Sales/AE (me + Laura) will offer a one-time credit/discount if NovaTek insists on assignment language for productization use.
3) Share SOC2 stub internally and prepare a telemetry field list for Hannah.

Can you draft language and the recommended redline positions? Timebox: can we get a first pass by EOD tomorrow? I’ll hold off on escalating to execs unless legal thinks it’s a material concession.

Thanks,
Stephanie

Steph — thanks for the clear note. Drafted two short clauses below that mirror the proposed compromise; I’ve included commentary for commercial alignment. If these read OK, I’ll insert them into a clean counterproposal (tracked) and we can push to DocuSign.

1) Feedback/Training Clause (proposed):
"Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, revocable feedback license to use Customer feedback and anonymized usage signals to improve Redwood’s services. Such license expressly excludes any right to (a) train, fine-tune, or otherwise create customer-specific model weights using Customer’s identifiable training data, and (b) redistribute Customer outputs as training datasets without Customer’s separate written consent (which may be delivered via a Data Use Addendum)."

Comment: This directly addresses NovaTek’s opt-in retrain ask while preserving Redwood’s ability to improve the platform from aggregated signals.

2) Deliverables / Assignment Carveout (proposed):
"Notwithstanding any other provision, Customer retains ownership of Customer Content and Outputs generated solely from Customer Content. Redwood shall not claim assignment of Customer Outputs for the purpose of commercializing Customer-specific productizations. For clarity, Redwood may propose separate commercial terms (including a license fee or subscription tier) under which additional productization rights may be granted in writing."

Comment: This avoids broad assignment language but gives a commercial pathway if NovaTek insists on productization rights. Sales can offer a one-time concession/credit tied to execution of the Data Use Addendum or higher-tier Dedicated plan.

Attachments: I’ve created a clean tracked counter (Novatek_OrderForm_redline_v4.pdf) and a short negotiation memo — both attached as stubs below. I also confirm SOC2_Type2_stub.pdf is available for their security team; Laura, please share the telemetry field list and I’ll prep legal-friendly wording.

Next steps:
- If Steph + Laura approve, I’ll insert these two clauses and send the counter to Alex with a concise negotiation memo and a DocuSign route.
- If NovaTek insists on assignment, escalate to execs for approval of the commercial concession (we propose: 10% one-time onboarding credit against first-year committed spend).

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
